summary: Read the implicit-transition receipt (a07650e44835449790f588dc30fb5df0, completed, tests_passed, exit 0, no changed target files), which carries all three transition cases in one invocation: indices 0-2 the explicit case (accepted as EntryConfChangeV2, apply panicking with config is already joint while still joint), 3-4 the Auto control (no panic, joint configuration left with voters [1 2 3 4]), and 5-7 the implicit case (accepted as EntryConfChangeV2, same panic, still joint), with both implicit comparisons holding and complete. I recorded a measured fact for the implicit case tied to indices 6 and 7 and revised the interpretation to widen the trigger from one explicit transition value to every non-Auto transition with an empty change set in a joint configuration, citing indices 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7. The defect account is otherwise unchanged: propose-time validation derives leave-joint from len(Changes)==0 while the apply path derives it from LeaveJoint, which also requires the Auto transition, so an accepted and replicated EntryConfChangeV2 panics the process in the application's ApplyConfChange call where the not-joint case is instead rejected with a log message and an entry rewrite; the Auto control shows the issue is the disagreement between the two tests rather than empty change sets as such. An application that rejects the change avoids the crash, no state corruption or safety violation is claimed, and the apply step was driven directly because a quorum-less instance cannot commit.
